Roofing in Fort Worth, Texas

Fort Worth tells homeowners in writing what a re-roof needs, from permits to drip edge. Call one free number any hour and get put through to an independent roofing company that takes Fort Worth calls.

A city that answers the roofing questions in writing

Roofing in Fort Worth, TX starts with a document most homeowners never open. The city's Development Services department publishes a residential roofing FAQ, and it settles several arguments that come up between homeowners, roofers and adjusters: when a permit is needed, whether old decking must go, and which edge details every new roof gets.

Fort Worth also has the storm record to explain why those questions come up so often. The May 1995 Mayfest supercell and the March 2000 downtown tornado both hit this city, and spring hail still rolls in from the west most years. When a whole street needs roofs at once, it helps to know the rules before the first knock on the door.

DFW Expert Roofers is not one of the roofing companies in Fort Worth. It is a free phone line. An automated assistant answers at any hour, asks about the damage and your part of town, and then hands the call to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Fort Worth calls. From there the roofer handles the inspection, the written price and the job itself, and it bills you, not the line.

Fort Worth's re-roofing rules, side by side

These points come from the City of Fort Worth roofing FAQ and its residential permitting page. The FAQ follows the 2021 International Residential Code as amended locally, so confirm the current version with Development Services before work starts.

Situation on a one or two family homeWhat the city saysWhat to ask the roofer
New shingles only, no decking replacedNo building permit needed, but the code limits how many shingle layers a roof may haveWill you tear off to the deck or lay over, and how many layers are on the roof now?
Any decking, sheathing, lathing, rafters or ridge boards replacedA building permit is requiredWho pulls the permit, and how is replacement decking priced?
Existing decking in good shapeA roof that met code when built still complies; sound sheathing does not have to be replacedCan I see photos of every sheet you plan to replace?
New decking going onNo new layer of decking over an existing layerWill the old decking come off where new decking goes on?
Thin decking on 24 inch rafters3/8 inch plywood or OSB is still allowed when the span rating is 24/0What span rating is on the panels you are using?
Drip edge and cricketsRequired when re-roofing if they are not already thereAre drip edge and any needed crickets listed in the written scope?
Ice barrier underlaymentNot required locally, since the area has no history of ice dammingIf you recommend it in valleys anyway, why, and what does it add?

Whoever pulls a Fort Worth building permit must hold a Contractor Registration with Development Services. The exception is a homeowner pulling a homestead permit for their own house, which this site does not suggest for roof work. Ask any roofer for the name its registration is under, and make sure the permit is filed under that same name.

Two storms Fort Worth still measures others against

Ask anyone who has lived in Tarrant County for a while about hail, and the Mayfest storm usually comes up. Here is what the National Weather Service records about the two big ones.

  • May 5, 1995, the Mayfest storm. A high-precipitation supercell moved in from west of the city and struck the Mayfest festival in Fort Worth around 7:10 p.m. The Weather Service lists hail to softball size, gusts near 70 mph and rain falling at up to 2.25 inches in 15 minutes. Its case study puts damage at about two billion dollars across Tarrant and Dallas counties, which still ranks it among the costliest hailstorms on record.
  • March 28, 2000, the downtown tornado. A tornado touched down about four miles west of downtown, followed West 7th Street, badly damaged the Cash America building and broke thousands of windows in downtown towers. Two people died. The same storms dropped hail that severely damaged roofs and cars in Lake Worth and Saginaw, according to the Weather Service review.

Neither storm is likely to repeat exactly, but they explain the pattern. Fort Worth sits on the western side of the metroplex, so spring storms building over the plains often reach it before they reach Dallas. A roof here can take hail that bruises shingles without leaving a mark you can see from the yard, which is why a careful roofer looks at vents, gutters and soft metal as well as the shingles themselves.

After a Fort Worth hailstorm

  1. Stay on the ground. Look from the yard and the street, and note any shingles, ridge caps or vent covers that came down.
  2. Photograph everything. Dented gutters, hail on the lawn, ceiling stains inside. Date the photos.
  3. Call your insurer. Ask how wind and hail claims work on your policy, how large the deductible is, and whether an older roof is paid out at full replacement value or depreciated value.
  4. Have one roofer look. Plenty of roofers look at storm damage without charging; ask about that when you are connected. Ask for photos of what it finds.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Historic districts add a step

Some Fort Worth homes sit in locally designated historic districts, and there the roof is part of the look the city protects. The design standards for the Fairmount/Southside Historic District, for example, say original tile and slate roofs are to be maintained, that a metal roof needs a Certificate of Appropriateness, and that standing seam metal may go on secondary slopes while R-panel and rib-panel profiles are not allowed. The city's historic roofing guidance ties a Certificate of Appropriateness to exterior work that requires a building permit. Carver Heights has its own published design guidelines.

If your house is in a historic district, call the city's historic preservation staff before you pick a material, and ask the roofer whether it has worked under these guidelines before. A shingle that matches what is there now is usually the simplest path; anything different should be cleared first.

Questions to ask before you hire a roofer in Fort Worth

  • What name is your Fort Worth Contractor Registration under, and will the permit be pulled in that name if decking is replaced?
  • How many shingle layers are on my roof now, and will you tear off to the deck?
  • If rotten or broken decking turns up, what does each sheet cost, and will I see a photo of it first?
  • Are drip edge, crickets and the underlayment listed in the written scope?
  • Will your insurance agent email me your liability certificate?
  • For a home in a historic district: have you worked under the city's preservation guidelines, and does my material need a Certificate of Appropriateness?
  • What does your workmanship warranty cover, and will you register the shingle manufacturer's warranty in my name?

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

Not sure whether your Fort Worth job needs a permit or whether the hail did enough damage for a claim? Call and describe the roof. The roofing company you are connected with sees it in person and puts its estimate in writing.

What Fort Worth homeowners ask about roofing

Is a city permit needed for a new roof in Fort Worth?

It depends on what comes off. The city's roofing FAQ says swapping shingles on a one or two family home does not need a building permit, although the code limits how many layers of shingles a roof may carry. Once any decking, sheathing, lathing boards, rafters or ridge boards are replaced, a building permit is required. Ask the roofer to state in the contract whether decking may be replaced and who will pull the permit if it is.

Must Fort Worth roofers register with the city?

Yes, if it pulls a permit. Fort Worth Development Services requires a valid Contractor Registration from any business that obtains a building permit, and the main exception is a homeowner working on their own homestead. With no state license for roofers in Texas, that registration is one of the few official records you can ask about. Our guide on checking a roofer in Texas lists the rest.

Will the whole roof deck have to be replaced to meet the new code?

Not according to the city. Fort Worth's roofing FAQ says a roof that met code when it was built still complies, and sheathing in good condition does not need to be replaced. It also notes that 3/8 inch plywood or OSB is still allowed on rafters 24 inches apart when the panel's span rating is 24/0. If a quote replaces every sheet, ask to see photos of the damaged ones and a price per sheet.

Is ice and water shield required on a Fort Worth roof?

The city's local amendments do not require an ice barrier underlayment, because the area has no history of ice damming. Drip edge and crickets are a different story: the FAQ says they are required when re-roofing if the roof does not already have them. A roofer may still suggest a membrane in valleys or around chimneys. Ask what it costs and why, and get it written into the scope.

What are the best roofing companies in Fort Worth?

This line does not rank or name companies, and no website can tell you which roofer will do your roof well. What you can check: the company's Fort Worth contractor registration, a certificate of liability insurance sent by its insurer, recent addresses you can drive by, and a written scope that follows the city's rules. Calling the number here connects you with one independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Fort Worth calls.

Is it legal for a Fort Worth roofer to cover my deductible?

No. Texas law bars a contractor from waiving, rebating or absorbing your deductible or inflating an estimate to cover it, and when insurance money funds a roofing contract of at least $1,000, the paperwork has to tell you the deductible is still yours. A roofer also may not negotiate your claim as a public adjuster. The Texas roof insurance claim guide walks through what to ask your insurer.
